missed.fact: The merged-app schema names (ITEM, TIME_SPAN, TRACKER...) do not exist in this repo. The table is `Entry` (`entries`). Its kinds and recurrence column are `EntryKind` and `recurrenceRule: RecurrenceRule?`. Recurrence is a sealed `RecurrenceRule` (it includes `Elastic(Period)`), not confirmed to be an RRULE string.

Recurrence exceptions already live on Entry rows (`originalEntryId` plus `isExceptionSkip`). HabitScheduleEdit therefore adds a second per-occurrence override mechanism for calendar habits, using EditScope.Occurrence/Day/Week/From/Extra. An item-level exception scheme would overlap it.

HabitBlock carries per-weekday time overrides packed into one text column (`SAT,SUN@480-630;…`). That is a second meaning in one field. It is a schedule rule of sorts, although it has no RRULE and no reminder.
HabitBlock has seeded default rows with fixed uids (block-morning … block-night) and updatedAt = EPOCH. Merge relies on these uids being the same on every device.
HabitScheduleEdit.target is a two-case enum stored as text (HABIT|BLOCK). It covers time blocks as well as habits. Its `changes` and `scope` are opaque strings kept verbatim.

A database row is a Page, and with syncToTasks a second row is written, an Entry (kind TASK, source DATABASE_SYNC) linked by Entry.sourceRowId. The two are two rows for one thing. The bound columns (done, date, due date, recurrence) are not stored in property_values while bound. They are proxied from the Entry, and crystallized back into property_values on unbind.

PageDatabase columns: id, uid, pageId, syncToTasks, donePropertyId?, deadlinePropertyId? (binds Entry.startDate), dueDatePropertyId?, recurrencePropertyId?, hue?, blockedByPropertyId?, labelId?, labelConfirmed, lastReviewedAt?, createdAt, updatedAt. `labelId` points at a Label, so page membership through a label overlaps the LABEL vocabulary. Labels are not fully merged: a page carrying the bound label becomes a member and, if syncToTasks is on, a task.

PropertyValue.value is an untyped String?. It holds NUMBER and DATE values with no timestamp of their own. It can hold the same idea as TRACKER_READING (a number in a database row) when the user builds such a database. The schema does not duplicate TRACKER_READING, and there is no logged-at column.

PropertyType.INTERVAL stores recurrence as an 'n:UNIT' string (e.g. 1:WEEK). When bound it becomes Entry.recurrenceRule (RecurrenceRule.Elastic). This is a second recurrence encoding that maps onto the item recurrence.

Tombstone schemes differ by entity. Page has deletedAt (soft delete). PageDatabase, Property, PropertyValue, PageDatabaseView, Block, PageRelation, PageCanvas, CanvasNode and CanvasEdge have no deletedAt. Pages sync through snapshot merge with delete-and-reinsert and a purge registry (PurgedKind PAGE, ENTRY, HABIT, PROPERTY). Properties are purged through that registry, so they have their own deletion path.
PageRevision has no uid and is never synced. It keeps the body that a sync merge overwrote (RevisionReason.MERGE). It is the only local record of the losing side of last-write-wins.
Block.checked (TODO blocks) is a second checkbox that never creates a task. It overlaps Entry completion in concept only.

CalendarLink has no uid and no id. Its key is the composite (calendarKey, entryUid, occurrence), and `occurrence` is an empty string for a series. Entry.providerEventId is a second device-local link to the system calendar that lives on the Entry row.
PropertyValue has no uid and no timestamp. It is identified by the pair (propertyId, rowPageId), which is a local id pair. It is rebuilt from uids on merge.
